title: Core Data: Create, Fetch & Sort
hints: Everything happens in a context: insert, mutate, delete, then `save()`.
`NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>(entityName: "Note")` with a predicate and sort descriptors.
Sort with two `NSSortDescriptor`s: priority descending, title ascending.
jsBridge: Core Data is an **object graph manager** over SQLite: you mutate managed objects in a context, then `save()`. The closest JS analogue is an ORM with a unit of work (like MikroORM's `em.flush()`), and contexts are thread-confined.

compass.q: An ORM unit of work (`em.persist(); em.flush()`) vs `context.insert; context.save()`: same model?
Why must all context work happen inside `perform`? What happens when you touch a context from the wrong thread?
Core Data vs SwiftData: what does SwiftData remove (the model file, `NSManagedObject` subclasses), and what does it keep?
Your app already ships Core Data. Migrate to SwiftData or keep it? What decides?
